newsitem.title: USA: TCI cancels spin-off of Liberty and others.
newsitem.headline: TCI cancels spin-off of Liberty and others.

text.p: Cable television giant Tele-Communications Inc. said Wednesday it would not spin off Liberty Media Corp. and two other subsidiaries because the Internal Revenue Service refused to rule on its request for tax-free status for the deals.

The company's decision to spin off Liberty Media, Tele-Communications International Inc. and Southern Satellite Systems Inc. depended in part upon a favourable ruling allowing the transactions to be tax-free to its shareholders.
The company, the nation's largest cable television operator, said it might consider refiling any or all of the ruling requests.

Tele-Communications said the IRS decision came after it was unable to meet the agency's request concerning the potential disposal of Tele-Communications stock by the estate of its founder, Bob Magness.

The agency wanted assurance from the estate that it would not dispose of Tele-Communications stock or stock of the spun-off corporations, or that if it did so, it would sell the shares in proportionately equal amounts, Tele-Communications said.
Tele-Communications said the estate was unable to make such assurances because of fiduciary duties to beneficiaries.
"Each of these assets is extremely valuable and TCI's stockholders will now continue to share in those values through their TCI Group and Liberty Media Group holdings, TCI said in a release.
